Australia's 2027 Mitsubishi Pajero Leaves Thai Plant, Customer Deliveries Expected Before Christmas
21 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi's 2027 model year Pajero is getting increasingly closer to Australian dealer lots and showrooms. The first Aussie units left the factory in Laem Chabang for terminal A5 of the port in the Chonburi province, where they were loaded onto big ships. In terms of customer deliveries, Mitsubishi Motors Australia claims December 2026. In the first instance, a 2.4-liter turbo diesel I4 has to suffice.
Thailand, Australia, and Japan are the first three key markets of the redesigned Pajero , which is a different animal from its predecessor in many respects. Availability will be expanded to just around 100 countries in 2027, and the Laem Chabang factory will serve all of them.
Part of the reason why Laem Chabang was chosen for 2027 Pajero assembly is the factory's experience producing the Triton pickup truck, which is also known as the L200 in certain parts of the world. The mid-size workhorse is mechanically related to the Pajero, hence the familiar inline-four turbo diesel hiding under the sport utility vehicle's hood.
A single-turbo affair is featured. Mitsubishi decided to replace the Triton's twin-stage turbo setup with a wide-range VGT for improved drivability and smoothness, with Mitsubishi engineers also tuning the 4N16 engine of the Pajero for low-speed controllability. Paired with an AdBlue system, the variable-geometry turbo diesel meets Euro 6d emission standards.
Prospective customers will enjoy up to 150 kilowatts (201 horsepower) and 480 Newton-meters (354 pound-feet) of twist, which are delivered to all four wheels by an eight-speed automatic transmission and Super Select 4WD-II with a dual-range transfer case. A rear diff lock is featured as well, as you would expect from an SUV with off-road chops.
Photo: Mitsubishi Its eight-speed auto is manufactured by Aisin, whereas the Super Select 4WD -II transfer case is an in-house Mitsubishi design. Listed with a 0.652 overdrive eighth gear, said tranny is perfectly suited to the 2.566 low-range reduction ratio of the transfer case. Of course, Pajero customers are presented with 2WD high range to improve fuel economy.
4H, 4HLc, and 4LLc also need mentioning, with HLc forcing a 50:50 torque split between the axles. LLc, meanwhile, keeps the center diff locked while engaging the 2.556:1 reduction gearset to multiply wheel torque for serious off-road scenarios like rock crawling. Rather than a mechanical rear diff lock, the front differential is an open design with brake-controlled locking capability.
Even the base GLS trim level with five seats gets all of this kit. Customers are further offered a three-row version of the GLS, along with the Exceed and GSR trims. Both upper trim levels are seven-seat exclusively. Before on-road costs and optional extras, prices range from AUD 68,490 all the way to AUD 84,990.
Mitsubishi's Australian division spent nearly five years developing accessories for the 2027 Pajero, including locally produced steel protection bars and towing kits. Roof racks, a snorkel, and side protection goodies also need mentioning. The body-on-frame sport utility vehicle is backed by the 10/10/10 Diamond Advantage program, which includes a 10-year warranty or 200,000 clicks of coverage.
That's 124,274 miles in the United Kingdom and the US of A. The second 10 stands for years of capped-price servicing, whereas the last 10 designates the years of roadside assistance. Under said warranty, customers are required to complete scheduled services at authorized Mitsubishi dealerships Down Under.
